text: Whether the assessed business identity and connected account ownership are supported by evidence.
Who owns or controls the borrower, its related-party balances, and supported guarantees.
Money entering and leaving the assessed accounts, with operating activity separated from transfers and funding.
Cash available to meet near-term obligations, including balance stability and periods of pressure.
How well revenue is supported, how recurring it is, and how reliably sales become cash.
Earnings retained after different layers of costs, distinguished from cash received.
Funds tied up in receivables, inventory and payables, and the timing of their conversion into cash.
The size, utilization and maturity of debt relative to the borrower's resources and operating activity.
The ability of evidenced cash flow to cover existing and proposed debt obligations.
Dependence on a small number of customers, suppliers, sales channels or income sources.
Supported asset security, competing claims and the value eligible to support an exposure.
Inconsistencies, duplicates and unsupported differences that warrant review. These observations do not establish fraud.
A consumer's supported income, essential costs and room for existing and proposed payments.
The recurrence, variability and continuity of a consumer's supported income streams.
Observed payment timeliness, returned payments and overdraft experience.
Obligations, inquiries and adverse events present in entitled credit or lender evidence.
Sales, customer activity, recurring subscriptions and the timing of settlement into bank cash.
Operating cost pressure and the business's ability to maintain inventory, fulfillment and supplier payments.
Supported tax obligations, arrears and filing evidence. This is not a legal compliance opinion.
Whether financial statements and books reconcile with each other and with bank evidence.
The completeness, freshness, classification and reconciliation of the evidence used in the assessment.
Cash and repayment capacity under the stated forecast or stress assumptions, rather than observed future outcomes.
Exposure to related parties and connected counterparties, including supported circular cash movements.
Changes in comparable financial measures since the saved monitoring baseline.
The business's age in completed months since its verified formation date.
The share of eligible disclosed connected accounts whose ownership positively matches the assessed borrower.
The portion of ownership in the assessed entity supported by non-overlapping ownership evidence.
The portion of receivables owed by related parties rather than unrelated customers.
The portion of the assessed exposure covered by documented collectible guarantees, capped at the exposure.
All posted money received in the assessed accounts before excluding transfers, borrowing or other non-revenue receipts.
All posted money leaving the assessed accounts before separating operating payments, transfers and financing activity.
The net change from posted cash movements after eliminating transfers within the consolidated account scope.
Cash received from supported operating activity, excluding borrowing, owner funding and internal transfers.
Cash paid for operations, excluding financing principal, capital expenditure and matched internal transfers.
The cash surplus or deficit from operating receipts and operating payments during the observation period.
Money received from another account within the assessed consolidation scope, rather than new external income.
Cash received from identified debt or equity funding, rather than trading activity.
The share of fully covered months in which net cash flow was positive.
How variable monthly net operating cash flow is relative to its typical magnitude. A higher value indicates less stable cash generation.
The relative improvement or deterioration in operating net cash flow against the preceding 90 days, using the prior period's absolute magnitude.
Supported cash balances available for use, excluding restricted funds.
The average consolidated closing cash balance over covered calendar days.
The lowest consolidated end-of-day cash balance observed in the period.
The number of covered days when the consolidated closing balance was negative. This differs from an overdraft in an individual account.
How many days of essential cash outgoings the unrestricted cash balance represents at the observed spending pace.
Current assets relative to current liabilities, indicating the balance-sheet resources available against near-term obligations.
Cash, short-term investments and eligible receivables relative to current liabilities, without relying on inventory.
Unrestricted cash and cash equivalents relative to current liabilities.
Revenue supported by evidence on the declared cash or accrual basis after applicable exclusions. It is not all money deposited.
The portion of verified revenue supported as recurring rather than one-off activity.
The relative increase or decrease in revenue against the comparable period in the prior year.
The relative increase or decrease in revenue against the immediately preceding 90-day period.
The variability of monthly revenue relative to average monthly revenue.
The portion of eligible gross sales value returned through refunds.
Disputed chargeback value relative to eligible processed sales value; this is not the probability of a future chargeback.
The portion of recognized sales supported by matched cash collections.
The portion of candidate operating-like receipts whose classification or supporting evidence remains unresolved.
The portion of verified revenue identified as nonrecurring.
Recognized revenue remaining after the cost of goods sold, before other operating costs.
Gross profit as a share of recognized revenue.
Earnings before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, supported by statement items without automatic discretionary addbacks.
EBITDA as a share of recognized revenue.
Recognized profit after the cost of goods sold and operating expenses, excluding financing costs.
Operating profit as a share of recognized revenue.
Recognized income remaining after all recognized expenses on the stated accounting basis.
Net profit as a share of recognized revenue.
Operating cash remaining after cash capital expenditures; borrowing proceeds do not establish free cash flow.
Period net profit relative to the average asset base. Annualization is only meaningful when explicitly stated.
The balance-sheet surplus or deficit of current assets over current liabilities at the same date.
The collection-time equivalent of trade receivables relative to credit sales for the period.
The payment-time equivalent of trade payables relative to credit purchases for the period.
The holding-time equivalent of inventory relative to the period's cost of goods sold.
The length of the operating funding cycle across inventory holding, customer collections and supplier payment timing.
The portion of collectible trade receivables whose contractual payment due dates have passed.
The portion of trade receivables more than 90 days past their payment due dates.
The portion of trade payables whose contractual payment due dates have passed.
How many times the period's cost of goods sold represents the average inventory balance.
Outstanding principal of resolved interest-bearing obligations within the supported debt scope.
Debt remaining after offsetting eligible unrestricted cash at the same assessment date.
Interest-bearing debt relative to total assets; non-debt liabilities are not included as debt.
Interest-bearing debt relative to positive equity. Nonpositive equity does not produce a usable ratio.
Net debt relative to supported trailing-12-month EBITDA, indicating debt size against earnings capacity.
The used portion of known committed revolving credit limits.
The portion of total debt principal contractually due within the next 365 days.
Principal contractually due within the next 90 days, including supported balloon payments.
Eligible cash available for debt service relative to existing and proposed contractual payments. A value of one represents coverage of the stated payments, not a lending approval.
Cash available against the explicitly defined set of fixed charges, including leases when applicable.
Supported earnings before interest and tax relative to interest expense for the same period.
Contractual principal, interest and mandatory debt fees on existing obligations over the assessment window.
Contractual payments and mandatory debt fees associated with the exact financing terms being assessed.
The combined, deduplicated contractual payments for existing and proposed obligations over the assessment window.
Cash left, or the shortfall, after existing and proposed contractual debt service.
Additional debt-service room at the institution's required coverage threshold. It is an analytical capacity amount, not a credit limit or offer.
Observed debt payments relative to operating cash receipts. This describes payment burden and does not replace contractual coverage analysis.
The portion of covered customer revenue attributable to the largest resolved customer.
The portion of covered customer revenue attributable to the five largest resolved customers, or all resolved customers when fewer than five exist.
The portion of covered supplier spending attributable to the largest resolved supplier.
The portion of covered sales-channel revenue attributable to the largest channel.
Customer revenue concentration on a zero-to-one scale. Higher values indicate greater dependence on fewer resolved customers.
Concentration of verified income among resolved income sources on a zero-to-one scale. Higher values indicate greater dependence on fewer sources.
The assessed facility exposure relative to the supported value of its collateral.
All known secured claims, including the proposed exposure, relative to the same collateral value.
Supported realizable collateral value after approved reductions relative to secured exposure.
Receivables that meet the institution's stated borrowing-base eligibility and concentration rules.
The portion of gross eligible collateral value excluded when arriving at supported realizable value.
The portion of eligible source value that remains unmatched across the compared evidence.
The portion of examined transaction records confirmed as duplicates before deduplication.
Distinct supported inconsistencies between comparable document fields. A contradiction is a review signal, not proof of fraud.
Distinct unresolved differences across supported borrower identity attributes. An absent attribute is not a mismatch.
How much declared income exceeds or falls below comparable verified income, expressed relative to verified income.
Supported recurring pretax consumer income expressed on a monthly basis. Net bank deposits alone do not establish this amount.
Supported recurring consumer income after deductions, expressed on a monthly basis.
Existing and proposed required monthly debt payments relative to verified gross monthly income.
Required monthly housing costs relative to verified gross monthly income, using the stated housing components.
Supported essential non-debt living expenditure on a monthly basis, with housing and debt counted only once.
Monthly net income left after essential spending, housing and existing and proposed debt payments.
The proposed required monthly payment relative to verified gross monthly income.
How many months of required outgoings the verified unrestricted liquid funds represent.
The number of distinct supported recurring income streams after resolving duplicate identities.
The variability of complete monthly verified income relative to its average, on a consistent gross or net basis.
The relative change in verified income against the comparable prior-year period.
The time since the most recent verified recurring income receipt as of the assessment date.
Elapsed days beyond the next expected recurring-income payment date without a matched receipt.
The portion of elapsed expected income periods with a supported receipt, given adequate account coverage.
Distinct returned-payment events supported as caused by insufficient funds, without counting the associated fee as another event.
Covered calendar days when at least one assessed account had a negative balance. Several overdrawn accounts on one day still represent one day.
The principal value of distinct returned-payment events, excluding duplicate fee records.
Supported obligations that are past due at the assessment date.
The longest supported payment delay among assessed obligations with known contractual dues and payment allocations.
The portion of elapsed eligible obligations paid by their contractual due dates.
Distinct open credit obligations found in entitled credit evidence or lender records.
Used revolving balances relative to reported credit limits in the entitled credit report, on its observation date.
Supported credit-inquiry events within the requested observation window.
Reported obligations meeting the institution's defined severe-delinquency criteria in the observation window.
Supported relevant insolvency or judgment events matched to the subject in entitled evidence.
Eligible sales before discounts and refunds, excluding taxes, on the stated sales basis.
Eligible sales after discounts, cancellations and refunds, excluding taxes.
Net eligible sales value per completed noncancelled order. This is an order measure, not a processor-payout measure.
The portion of purchasing customers who completed more than one purchase in the defined cohort.
Contracted recurring subscription revenue expressed on a monthly basis. It does not guarantee collection.
The portion of opening recurring revenue retained after churn and contraction, without counting expansion.
Recurring revenue retained from the opening customer cohort after churn, contraction and expansion.
The amount-weighted elapsed time between captured sales and their matched bank settlements.
Payroll cash costs, including supported employer costs, relative to verified revenue.
The relative change in payroll cost against the comparable prior-year period.
The portion of observed eligible item-days when sellable inventory was out of stock.
The portion of eligible fulfilled orders completed by their promised dates.
The amount-weighted lateness of settled supplier bills against their contractual due dates, with early payments treated as zero delay.
Supported outstanding assessed tax obligations at the assessment date, distinguished from estimates.
Supported assessed tax obligations that remain unpaid after their due dates.
Due assessed taxes supported as covered by allocated payments for the same period.
The portion of known required filings supported by filing evidence. This is evidence coverage, not a compliance conclusion.
The portion of eligible bank transaction value matched to accounting evidence for the same scope and period.
The amount by which a balance sheet fails to reconcile assets with liabilities and equity.
Supported material accounting adjustments relative to the magnitude of activity before those adjustments.
The elapsed time between the accounting period end and its supported closing or finalization date.
The portion of declared relevant accounts included in the assessment. It does not establish that every external account is known.
Days with complete evidence across the required source and account set, accounting for known gaps.
The portion of required sources older than their configured freshness tolerances.
The portion of eligible posted, deduplicated transaction records without a supported classification.
The portion of eligible transaction value supported as reconciled across evidence.
The lowest modeled closing cash balance within the specified forecast horizon.
Debt-service coverage under the stated stress scenario and its existing and proposed payment assumptions.
Consumer income remaining after essential, housing and debt outgoings under the stated stress scenario.
The modeled cash deficit against the explicitly required liquidity floor, with no deficit represented as zero.
The modeled reduction in revenue at which the specified capacity threshold is first breached.
The portion of operating cash receipts attributable to identified related parties.
The uniquely attributed value of evidence-supported cash paths that return funds through connected parties or accounts. This alone does not establish misconduct.
The portion of covered counterparty exposure attributable to evidence-linked counterparties.
The relative increase or decrease in comparable revenue since the saved monitoring baseline.
The money amount by which unrestricted cash has changed since the saved monitoring baseline.
The absolute change in the debt-service coverage ratio since the saved baseline, rather than a relative percentage change.
The relative increase or decrease in total debt since the saved monitoring baseline.
The number of eligible posted transaction records, counting each current resource version once.
The number of posted external sales receipts in the observed activity.
Cash supplied by owners from outside the assessed account scope.
Cash paid out to owners, distinguished from operating expenses and internal transfers.
Cash received from borrowing outside the assessed account scope.
Actual observed external debt-payment debits, including principal and any lender charges included in those debits. This is not the contractual payment schedule.
Observed external cash payments classified as financial fees in the transaction evidence.
Cash removed from the accounts through identified withdrawals; the withdrawal alone does not establish its later use.
Observed external cash payments classified as payroll.
Observed cash payments explicitly identified as inventory purchases.
Cash sent to other accounts within the assessed consolidation scope.
Operating cash spending relative to operating cash receipts. A value above one means spending exceeds receipts for the period.
The absolute change in the operating spending-to-receipts ratio against the preceding 90 days. It is a change in ratio units, not a relative growth rate.
The typical time between distinct dates with operating receipts.
How irregular the gaps between operating-receipt dates are, expressed in days.
How widely operating-receipt dates vary within the calendar month. This describes calendar timing, not receipt amounts.
Fully covered calendar months with no operating receipts. This is a cash-receipt observation and does not prove zero accrual revenue.
The variability of complete monthly operating cash receipts relative to their average amount.
The relative change in operating cash receipts against the preceding 90 days.
The time from the most recent operating receipt to the last included observation date, rather than to the date you retrieve the result.
The relative change in operating cash payments against the preceding 90 days.
The spread of daily consolidated closing balances, expressed as a money amount.
The variability of daily closing balances relative to the absolute average balance.
The highest consolidated daily closing balance in the covered period.
The middle consolidated daily closing balance, representing a typical covered day with less influence from extremes.
The number of covered days when consolidated closing cash was below the explicitly specified liquidity floor.
The money amount by which closing cash has increased or decreased from the closing balance 90 days earlier.
Distinct cash-pressure episodes beginning with a one-day decline of at least 20 percent from a positive prior closing balance. Overlapping episodes are not counted again.
The time taken to regain the pre-shock closing balance for the most recent cash-shock episode.
Cash-shock episodes that remain unresolved at the end of the observation window under the same 20 percent decline definition.
The portion of observed external cash outflows attributable to debt service.
The number of distinct observed active financing facilities after resolving duplicate facility identities.
Observed active facilities funded during the 90 days ending at the assessment time.
Supported total debt relative to observed operating receipts over the trailing year.
The portion of external cash inflows assigned to unknown or other categories.
Number of observed non-draft, non-void customer invoices with a positive balance still owed.
Total outstanding value of observed non-draft, non-void customer invoices. This does not establish the whole business's balance.
Outstanding money owed on customer invoices that are not yet past due, including amounts due today. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Number of open customer invoices that are not yet past due, including amounts due today. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Portion of observed outstanding value on customer invoices that are not yet past due, including amounts due today. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Outstanding money owed on customer invoices that are 1-30 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Number of open customer invoices that are 1-30 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Portion of observed outstanding value on customer invoices that are 1-30 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Outstanding money owed on customer invoices that are 31-60 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Number of open customer invoices that are 31-60 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Portion of observed outstanding value on customer invoices that are 31-60 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Outstanding money owed on customer invoices that are 61-90 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Number of open customer invoices that are 61-90 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Portion of observed outstanding value on customer invoices that are 61-90 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Outstanding money owed on customer invoices that are 91-120 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Number of open customer invoices that are 91-120 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Portion of observed outstanding value on customer invoices that are 91-120 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Outstanding money owed on customer invoices that are more than 120 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Number of open customer invoices that are more than 120 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Portion of observed outstanding value on customer invoices that are more than 120 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Lateness of open customer invoices, weighted by outstanding value. Amounts not yet overdue contribute zero days.
Age of the most overdue open customer invoice. No open documents is not applicable.
Portion of observed outstanding value attributable to the largest identified customer.
Average time from issue to full collection for observed customer invoices fully paid within the reporting window.
Middle time from issue to full collection for observed customer invoices fully paid within the reporting window.
90th-percentile time from issue to full collection for observed customer invoices fully paid within the reporting window.
Portion of observed customer invoices fully paid in the window that were paid after their due dates.
Average lateness among late customer invoices fully paid in the window. On-time documents are excluded.
Portion of observed outstanding value on customer invoices explicitly marked partially paid.
Source-reported credits applied to customer invoices issued in the window, relative to their original totals. This follows the issue cohort, not when credits or write-offs occurred.
Number of observed non-draft, non-void supplier bills with a positive balance still owed.
Total outstanding value of observed non-draft, non-void supplier bills. This does not establish the whole business's balance.
Outstanding money owed on supplier bills that are not yet past due, including amounts due today. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Number of open supplier bills that are not yet past due, including amounts due today. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Portion of observed outstanding value on supplier bills that are not yet past due, including amounts due today. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Outstanding money owed on supplier bills that are 1-30 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Number of open supplier bills that are 1-30 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Portion of observed outstanding value on supplier bills that are 1-30 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Outstanding money owed on supplier bills that are 31-60 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Number of open supplier bills that are 31-60 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Portion of observed outstanding value on supplier bills that are 31-60 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Outstanding money owed on supplier bills that are 61-90 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Number of open supplier bills that are 61-90 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Portion of observed outstanding value on supplier bills that are 61-90 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Outstanding money owed on supplier bills that are 91-120 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Number of open supplier bills that are 91-120 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Portion of observed outstanding value on supplier bills that are 91-120 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Outstanding money owed on supplier bills that are more than 120 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Number of open supplier bills that are more than 120 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Portion of observed outstanding value on supplier bills that are more than 120 days past due. Age is measured from the payment due date.
Lateness of open supplier bills, weighted by outstanding value. Amounts not yet overdue contribute zero days.
Age of the most overdue open supplier bill. No open documents is not applicable.
Portion of observed outstanding value attributable to the largest identified supplier.
Average time from issue to full payment for observed supplier bills fully paid within the reporting window.
Middle time from issue to full payment for observed supplier bills fully paid within the reporting window.
90th-percentile time from issue to full payment for observed supplier bills fully paid within the reporting window.
Portion of observed supplier bills fully paid in the window that were paid after their due dates.
Average lateness among late supplier bills fully paid in the window. On-time documents are excluded.
Portion of observed outstanding value on supplier bills explicitly marked partially paid.
Source-reported credits applied to supplier bills issued in the window, relative to their original totals. This follows the issue cohort, not when credits or write-offs occurred.
Portion of observed orders placed in the window that are cancelled.
Portion of observed noncancelled orders placed in the window with a positive discount.
Discount value relative to source-reported subtotals on observed noncancelled orders. The source subtotal convention matters; this is not a profit margin.
Number of observed noncancelled orders that are paid but remain wholly or partially unfulfilled.
Full current value of paid orders that remain wholly or partially unfulfilled. Partial fulfillment does not mean this entire value is undelivered.
Age of the oldest paid, wholly or partially unfulfilled order among observed orders placed in the reporting window.
Concentration of observed noncancelled order value across sales channels. Higher zero-to-one values indicate greater dependence on fewer channels.
Concentration of observed noncancelled order value across identified customers. Higher zero-to-one values indicate greater dependence on fewer customers.
Concentration of observed noncancelled order value across identified locations. Higher zero-to-one values indicate greater dependence on fewer locations.
Number of observed payouts created in the window and currently awaiting processing. A payout status alone does not establish reconciled bank cash.
Source-reported net value of observed payouts created in the window and currently awaiting processing. A payout status alone does not establish reconciled bank cash.
Number of observed payouts created in the window and currently in transit. A payout status alone does not establish reconciled bank cash.
Source-reported net value of observed payouts created in the window and currently in transit. A payout status alone does not establish reconciled bank cash.
Number of observed payouts created in the window and currently reported as paid. A payout status alone does not establish reconciled bank cash.
Source-reported net value of observed payouts created in the window and currently reported as paid. A payout status alone does not establish reconciled bank cash.
Number of observed payouts created in the window and currently reported as failed. A payout status alone does not establish reconciled bank cash.
Source-reported net value of observed payouts created in the window and currently reported as failed. A payout status alone does not establish reconciled bank cash.
Number of observed payouts created in the window and currently reported as cancelled. A payout status alone does not establish reconciled bank cash.
Source-reported net value of observed payouts created in the window and currently reported as cancelled. A payout status alone does not establish reconciled bank cash.
Portion of observed payouts created in the window that failed. The assessed population also includes pending attempts.
Middle lateness of paid payouts against their expected arrival dates, with early arrivals counted as zero delay. This is not total payout-processing time.
90th-percentile lateness of paid payouts against their expected arrival dates, with early arrivals counted as zero delay. This is not total payout-processing time.
Explicitly reported processing fees relative to captured payment value. Missing fees are not estimated from a nominal fee schedule.
Portion of payments captured in the window with a positive refunded amount. This follows the capture cohort rather than the date of refund events.
Middle elapsed time from payment capture to settlement among observed settled payments captured in the window.
90th-percentile elapsed time from payment capture to settlement among observed settled payments captured in the window.
Number of observed disputes opened in the window and currently requiring a response.
Number of observed disputes opened in the window and currently under review.
Number of observed disputes opened in the window and currently explicitly recorded as won.
Number of observed disputes opened in the window and currently explicitly recorded as lost.
Number of observed disputes opened in the window and currently closed without inferring whether they were won or lost.
Portion of explicitly won or lost disputes recorded as won. Unresolved and generically closed disputes do not count as wins.
Value disputed in cases requiring a response or under review. This is unresolved exposure, not expected loss.
Number of observed disputes still requiring a response after their response deadlines.
Recorded carrying value of observed inventory explicitly owned by the business. Carrying value is not liquidation value or confirmed collateral eligibility.
Recorded carrying value of observed inventory explicitly held under a consignment arrangement. Carrying value is not liquidation value or confirmed collateral eligibility.
Recorded carrying value of observed inventory explicitly classified as third-party inventory. Carrying value is not liquidation value or confirmed collateral eligibility.
Recorded carrying value for inventory already expired before the assessment date. Missing expiry dates do not establish nonperishability.
Number of recorded positions for inventory already expired before the assessment date. Missing expiry dates do not establish nonperishability.
Share of total observed carrying value for inventory already expired before the assessment date. Missing expiry dates do not establish nonperishability.
Recorded carrying value for inventory expiring from today through 30 days ahead. Missing expiry dates do not establish nonperishability.
Number of recorded positions for inventory expiring from today through 30 days ahead. Missing expiry dates do not establish nonperishability.
Share of total observed carrying value for inventory expiring from today through 30 days ahead. Missing expiry dates do not establish nonperishability.
Recorded carrying value for inventory expiring 31-60 days ahead. Missing expiry dates do not establish nonperishability.
Number of recorded positions for inventory expiring 31-60 days ahead. Missing expiry dates do not establish nonperishability.
Share of total observed carrying value for inventory expiring 31-60 days ahead. Missing expiry dates do not establish nonperishability.
Recorded carrying value for inventory expiring 61-90 days ahead. Missing expiry dates do not establish nonperishability.
Number of recorded positions for inventory expiring 61-90 days ahead. Missing expiry dates do not establish nonperishability.
Share of total observed carrying value for inventory expiring 61-90 days ahead. Missing expiry dates do not establish nonperishability.
Number of inventory positions with negative recorded on-hand quantity. It does not combine quantities of unrelated products.
Portion of observed inventory carrying value represented by reserved quantities within each position. Reservations do not establish a completed sale.
Magnitude of source-recorded cost associated with inventory write-offs in the window. An adjustment or return does not automatically establish shrinkage.
Magnitude of source-recorded cost associated with inventory adjustments in the window. An adjustment or return does not automatically establish shrinkage.
Magnitude of source-recorded cost associated with inventory returns in the window. An adjustment or return does not automatically establish shrinkage.
Observed outstanding loan principal on facilities maturing from the assessment date up to, but excluding, 7 days later. This is maturity exposure, not the amount of scheduled installments.
Remaining payments on supplied installments due from the assessment date up to, but excluding, 7 days later. It does not assert that all external debt was supplied.
Observed outstanding loan principal on facilities maturing from the assessment date up to, but excluding, 30 days later. This is maturity exposure, not the amount of scheduled installments.
Remaining payments on supplied installments due from the assessment date up to, but excluding, 30 days later. It does not assert that all external debt was supplied.
Observed outstanding loan principal on facilities maturing from the assessment date up to, but excluding, 60 days later. This is maturity exposure, not the amount of scheduled installments.
Remaining payments on supplied installments due from the assessment date up to, but excluding, 60 days later. It does not assert that all external debt was supplied.
Observed outstanding loan principal on facilities maturing from the assessment date up to, but excluding, 90 days later. This is maturity exposure, not the amount of scheduled installments.
Remaining payments on supplied installments due from the assessment date up to, but excluding, 90 days later. It does not assert that all external debt was supplied.
Remaining amount on observed installments whose due dates are before the assessment date.
Number of observed past-due installments with a positive amount still owed.
Portion of observed loan principal explicitly subject to variable interest rates. Unknown rate types are not treated as fixed.
Portion of observed outstanding loan principal owed to the largest identified creditor.
Distinct customers with an observed active subscription at the assessment time. This is current membership, not a historical retention measure.
Portion of observed active or past-due subscriptions recorded as past due.

One next recurring billing amount per observed active subscription due from the assessment date up to, but excluding, 7 days later. It is not a collection forecast and excludes additional future cycles and usage charges.

One next recurring billing amount per observed active subscription due from the assessment date up to, but excluding, 30 days later. It is not a collection forecast and excludes additional future cycles and usage charges.

One next recurring billing amount per observed active subscription due from the assessment date up to, but excluding, 60 days later. It is not a collection forecast and excludes additional future cycles and usage charges.

One next recurring billing amount per observed active subscription due from the assessment date up to, but excluding, 90 days later. It is not a collection forecast and excludes additional future cycles and usage charges.
Portion of observed posted or reversed journals with an explicit link to the journal they reverse. Missing links do not prove no reversals occurred.
Portion of observed posted or reversed journals linked to a source document. An absent link alone does not establish fraud or manual origin.
Portion of observed posted or reversed journals explicitly identified as manual entries. Narrative text is not used to guess manual origin.
Number of supplied reconciliation links between orders and payments.
Portion of supplied links between orders and payments marked matched. This describes link status, not the share of all transaction value reconciled.
Number of supplied links between orders and payments explicitly marked as conflicting.
Number of supplied reconciliation links between payments and payouts.
Portion of supplied links between payments and payouts marked matched. This describes link status, not the share of all transaction value reconciled.
Number of supplied links between payments and payouts explicitly marked as conflicting.
Number of supplied reconciliation links between payouts and bank transactions.
Portion of supplied links between payouts and bank transactions marked matched. This describes link status, not the share of all transaction value reconciled.
Number of supplied links between payouts and bank transactions explicitly marked as conflicting.
Number of supplied reconciliation links between invoices and bank transactions.
Portion of supplied links between invoices and bank transactions marked matched. This describes link status, not the share of all transaction value reconciled.
Number of supplied links between invoices and bank transactions explicitly marked as conflicting.
Number of supplied reconciliation links between bank transactions and journals.
Portion of supplied links between bank transactions and journals marked matched. This describes link status, not the share of all transaction value reconciled.
Number of supplied links between bank transactions and journals explicitly marked as conflicting.
Total amount for inflow depository-account cash, selecting
balance adjustments,
over last 30 complete days.
A supported adjustment to account balance that is not assigned to a more specific economic activity.
Total money amount of the selected posted activity in one direction. It is not a net cash-flow or revenue figure.
Share of directional amount for inflow depository-account cash, selecting
Selected activity as a share of all posted value in the same account context, currency, direction and period.
Transaction count for inflow depository-account cash, selecting
Number of distinct current posted transactions in the selection.
over last 365 complete days.
over last 90 complete days.
posting corrections,
A correction to a previous posting, with its relationship retained where supported.
noncash foreign-exchange revaluation,
A noncash change from revaluing foreign-currency balances, not a cash receipt or payment.
Days with activity for inflow depository-account cash, selecting
adjustments and corrections,
over current calendar month through the last complete day.
Corrections, reversals and other supported account postings that require separate treatment from new economic activity.

Separately identified mortgage interest, distinct from repayment of borrowed principal.
overdraft interest,
Separately identified overdraft interest, distinct from repayment of borrowed principal.
related-party borrowing interest,
Separately identified related-party borrowing interest, distinct from repayment of borrowed principal.
revolving-facility interest,
Separately identified revolving-facility interest, distinct from repayment of borrowed principal.
term-loan interest,
Separately identified term-loan interest, distinct from repayment of borrowed principal.
unspecified interest paid,
Supported interest paid without a more specific borrowing-product classification.
financial costs,
Charges associated with banking, payment processing and financing, rather than borrowed principal.
bridge-loan repayments,
Settlement of obligations through bridge-loan repayments. The posting may combine principal and charges unless a supported split is available.
credit-card balance settlements,
Payment of a credit-card balance. The bank-side cash outflow and issuer-side settlement are not another purchase and must not double count the original card spending.
equipment-finance payments,
Settlement of obligations through equipment-finance payments. The posting may combine principal and charges unless a supported split is available.
factoring settlements,
Settlement of obligations through factoring settlements. The posting may combine principal and charges unless a supported split is available.
government-loan repayments,
Settlement of obligations through government-loan repayments. The posting may combine principal and charges unless a supported split is available.
invoice-finance repayments,
Settlement of obligations through invoice-finance repayments. The posting may combine principal and charges unless a supported split is available.
finance-lease payments,
Settlement of obligations through finance-lease payments. The posting may combine principal and charges unless a supported split is available.
merchant cash-advance remittances,
Settlement of obligations through merchant cash-advance remittances. The posting may combine principal and charges unless a supported split is available.
debt and facility settlements,
Payments that settle debt or a financing facility. Components remain combined unless evidence supports a principal, interest or fee split.
mortgage payments,
Settlement of obligations through mortgage payments. The posting may combine principal and charges unless a supported split is available.
supported principal-only repayments,
Repayment explicitly supported as principal only, without assumed interest or fee components.
related-party loan repayments,
Settlement of obligations through related-party loan repayments. The posting may combine principal and charges unless a supported split is available.
revolving-facility repayments,
Settlement of obligations through revolving-facility repayments. The posting may combine principal and charges unless a supported split is available.
term-loan payments,
Settlement of obligations through term-loan payments. The posting may combine principal and charges unless a supported split is available.
unspecified debt-service payments,
Supported debt-service payments whose facility type or component split is unresolved.
dividends paid,
Dividends paid to equity holders.
owner draws,
Funds withdrawn by an owner as a distribution, rather than supported wages or supplier costs.
owner and equity distributions,
Cash or value distributed to owners and equity investors, distinguished from ordinary operating costs.
partner distributions,
Distributions paid to partners in their ownership capacity.
capital returned to owners,
Capital returned to owners or investors, distinguished from ordinary expenses.
share repurchases,
Funds paid to repurchase the entity's own shares.
business acquisition,
Payments for business acquisition recorded as supported asset or investment activity rather than an ordinary operating purchase.
term-deposit placements,
Funds placed into a term-deposit investment.
equipment acquisition,
Payments for equipment acquisition recorded as supported asset or investment activity rather than an ordinary operating purchase.
capitalized technology hardware,
Payments for capitalized technology hardware recorded as supported asset or investment activity rather than an ordinary operating purchase.
intellectual-property acquisition,
Payments for intellectual-property acquisition recorded as supported asset or investment activity rather than an ordinary operating purchase.
capitalized leasehold improvements,
Payments for capitalized leasehold improvements recorded as supported asset or investment activity rather than an ordinary operating purchase.
loans advanced,
Funds lent to another party, creating a supported loan asset rather than an operating expense.
asset acquisition payments,
Payments to acquire supported assets, make investments or advance loans.
other documented investment payments,
Other supported investment or asset-acquisition payments without a more specific classification.
real-estate acquisition,
Payments for real-estate acquisition recorded as supported asset or investment activity rather than an ordinary operating purchase.
financial-security purchases,
Payments for financial-security purchases recorded as supported asset or investment activity rather than an ordinary operating purchase.
capitalized software,
Payments for capitalized software recorded as supported asset or investment activity rather than an ordinary operating purchase.
vehicle acquisition,
Payments for vehicle acquisition recorded as supported asset or investment activity rather than an ordinary operating purchase.
customer refunds paid,
Funds returned to a customer for an earlier payment or sale.
business levies,
Payments or charges identified as business levies under the applicable jurisdiction.
corporate income tax,
Payments or charges identified as corporate income tax under the applicable jurisdiction.
customs duties,
Payments or charges identified as customs duties under the applicable jurisdiction.
employer payroll taxes,
Payroll taxes borne by the employer, distinct from employee withholding remittances.
excise taxes,
Payments or charges identified as excise taxes under the applicable jurisdiction.
franchise taxes,
Statutory franchise-tax payments, distinct from commercial royalties paid to a franchisor.
gst and hst remittances,
Remittances of Canadian goods and services tax or harmonized sales tax collected or owed.
income-tax installments,
Payments or charges identified as income-tax installments under the applicable jurisdiction.
tax interest,
Payments or charges identified as tax interest under the applicable jurisdiction.
taxes and public remittances,
Tax payments, statutory remittances and related public charges. The category does not establish filing compliance or tax deductibility.
payroll tax withholding remittances,
Amounts withheld from employee pay and remitted to the tax authority, distinct from the employer's own payroll taxes.
tax penalties,
Payments or charges identified as tax penalties under the applicable jurisdiction.
property taxes,
Payments or charges identified as property taxes under the applicable jurisdiction.
pst and qst remittances,
Remittances of provincial sales tax or Quebec sales tax.
sales and use taxes,
Payments or charges identified as sales and use taxes under the applicable jurisdiction.
employer statutory social contributions,
Payments or charges identified as employer statutory social contributions under the applicable jurisdiction.
unspecified tax remittances,
Supported tax remittances without a more specific tax classification.
vat remittances,
Remittances of value-added tax under the applicable jurisdiction.
other withholding-tax remittances,
Other tax amounts withheld and remitted on behalf of a recipient.
escrow funding paid,
Funds paid into or through an escrow-related arrangement.
